sub: Technology block (e): API tests everyone on the team can read

title: What Is Karate?
desc: An open-source test automation framework built for APIs and web services

items: Open-source tool for test automation, designed specifically for API tests and web services
Tests are written in a simple, readable syntax based on Gherkin — accessible even to non-programmers
Supports functional and performance tests, plus API, UI and end-to-end testing in one tool
Integrates quickly into CI/CD pipelines — known for efficiency and ease of use
For our domain: every contract from Modules 7 and 10 (telemetry, clearance, airspace view) is a natural Karate target

title: Example 1: The Airspace Read Model
desc: A complete Karate feature file against the Module 10 query side — no Java code required

body.code: Feature: airspace read model (Module 10, query side) Background: * url baseUrl Scenario: current view of a control zone Given path 'airspace', 'EDDS-CTR-S' When method get Then status 200 And match response == { zoneId: 'EDDS-CTR-S', activeClearances: '#[] #object', updatedAt: '#string' } And match each response.activeClearances == { droneId: '#string', until: '#string' } Scenario: unknown zone Given path 'airspace', 'NOWHERE' When method get Then status 404
body.note: match validates the whole JSON payload structurally — '#string' and '#[] #object' are fuzzy matchers (any string, any array of objects); match each checks every element. The entire read-model contract, in eight lines a non-programmer can review.

title: Example 2: Clearance — Granted, Then Refused
desc: Chaining requests: the 201 / 409 pair from the Module 7 contract, proven in one scenario

body.code: Feature: flight clearance (Module 7 contract, Module 10 command side) Background: * url baseUrl * def mission = """ { droneId: 'mini4-01', zoneId: 'EDDS-CTR-S', from: '2026-08-26T10:00:00Z', until: '2026-08-26T10:30:00Z' } """ Scenario: first request in a free volume is granted, the second one conflicts Given path 'clearances' And request mission When method post Then status 201 * def clearanceId = response.id Given path 'clearances' And request { droneId: 'mini4-02', zoneId: 'EDDS-CTR-S', from: '2026-08-26T10:10:00Z', until: '2026-08-26T10:20:00Z' } When method post Then status 409 And match response.conflictsWith == clearanceId
body.note: State flows between steps: the id captured from the first response is asserted in the second. The spec in Module 7 promised '201 granted, 409 conflict' — this file is the proof, and it runs against the real service.

title: Same Feature File, Three Jobs
desc: Functional test on your laptop, load test in Gatling, gate in CI — without rewriting a line

body.code: // Load test: karate-gatling reuses the feature file (Scala) class TelemetryLoad extends Simulation { val fixes = scenario("1,000 drones at 1 Hz") .exec(karateFeature("classpath:telemetry/post-fix.feature")) setUp(fixes.inject(rampUsers(1000) during (60.seconds))) } # CI gate (GitHub Actions): the contract runs before anything flies - run: mvn test -Dkarate.env=ci - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: { name: karate-report, path: target/karate-reports/ }

items: Functional — does the service honour the contract? Green or red per scenario, HTML report per run
Load — at what rate does POST /fixes start to queue? The number Module 8 promised (few threads, thousands of streams) gets measured, not believed
CI — a red contract blocks the merge: this is No Green, No Props for the backend (Module 2)
Karate writes API tests in readable Gherkin — no Java required, so the whole team can read and run them
match checks a whole payload structurally; fuzzy matchers (#string, #[] #object) keep tests stable when data changes
Chaining requests — capture an id, assert it later — expresses multi-step contracts like granted-then-conflict in one scenario
One feature file serves three jobs: functional test, Gatling load test, CI gate
Every contract from Modules 7 and 10 gets a feature file before it gets traffic — the Safety & Testing gate, API edition
